we have shown that human malignant tumours are capable of living in organ culture, that the conditions for their survival and growth have been established, and that we have shown their dependence on factors of their own or of other species which favour their survival and growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of organ culture of human tumors, which allows for the maintenance of the initial characteristics of these tumors, is a useful tool for studying the factors that control the growth of malignant tumors.
we have developed a method that allows for the study of factors that promote the growth of human cancer in vitro.

the use of organoids as a model for studying the effects of anticancer drugs is limited by the fact that they do not accurately reflect the complexity and heterogeneity of the human tumor microenvironment.
